objective: Genuine ABP follower growth from owned article adaptations
design: 24 offline concepts across eight articles; select 12 distinct reviewed stories for a proposed rolling launch, then independently confirm promising patterns. Not randomized viewer A/B testing.
format_assignments: Unassigned until script and creative review; balance topic/time blocks before publication.
metrics_caveat: Per-Reel follows not listed in current Meta media Insights API table. Missing attribution prevents automated follower-conversion winner selection.

concepts.draft_hook: Up 50%. Down 40%. You still lose money.
concepts.explanatory_task: Animate 1 × 1.5 × 0.6 = 0.9; distinguish sequential outcomes from one-bet expectation.

concepts.draft_hook: The average can rise while most players lose.
concepts.explanatory_task: Contrast people across one period with one person over time; never present the historical 94/100 simulation as a universal rate.

concepts.draft_hook: An attractive bet can become a dangerous habit.
concepts.explanatory_task: Show why fraction of wealth exposed changes the path; use explicitly hypothetical stakes.

concepts.draft_hook: A fair bet can have an optimal stake of zero.
concepts.explanatory_task: Explain a fair 50/50 double-or-lose game and the zero Kelly fraction, without personal investment advice.

concepts.draft_hook: Even generous odds do not mean bet everything.
concepts.explanatory_task: Derive 45% only for the article hypothetical: 50% win chance, 10-to-1 net profit, full stake lost otherwise.

concepts.draft_hook: A precise formula can hide a fragile guess.
concepts.explanatory_task: Show how changing assumed probability changes sizing; label estimates and do not reuse old startup failure statistics as current.

concepts.draft_hook: Before a project starts, imagine it has already failed.
concepts.explanatory_task: Contrast an assumed failure with asking what might go wrong; attribute the method.

concepts.source_anchor: everyone must participate and share their ideas
concepts.draft_hook: Your loudest teammate may be hiding your biggest risk.
concepts.explanatory_task: Show a round-robin of one concern per person, without claiming a quantified success effect.

concepts.source_anchor: a few minutes to write down everything
concepts.draft_hook: Give people a few minutes before the debate begins.
concepts.explanatory_task: Illustrate individual written concerns before discussion; distinguish the method from proof it always improves results.

concepts.draft_hook: More research can make you more confident without making you more right.
concepts.explanatory_task: Explain the cited study with attribution and scope; recheck its primary paper before writing final study claims.

concepts.draft_hook: Five headlines may be only one piece of evidence.
concepts.explanatory_task: Use an explicitly invented example of several reports repeating one underlying source.

concepts.draft_hook: If you could keep only five facts, which would you choose?
concepts.explanatory_task: Present the article proposed decision exercise; do not claim it is a proven investing strategy.

concepts.draft_hook: What happens when participants can guess your hypothesis?
concepts.explanatory_task: Explain a design concern using the cited archival critique; verify the primary paper and avoid overgeneralizing.

concepts.source_anchor: clear instructions for how to create it
concepts.draft_hook: Were the prison guards only reacting to their situation?
concepts.explanatory_task: Attribute the archival criticism and distinguish records from the author interpretation; no fabricated prison footage.

concepts.draft_hook: A famous result still needs someone to check the archives.
concepts.explanatory_task: Focus on replication incentives; do not equate one contested study with all psychology being false.

concepts.draft_hook: A stock story can change before the business does.
concepts.explanatory_task: Use the dated 2018 Match example only after checking contemporary primary records; clearly label its date.

concepts.source_anchor: Of course, stories can go both ways
concepts.angle: A story is not a forecast
concepts.draft_hook: A comeback-shaped story does not guarantee a comeback.
concepts.explanatory_task: Contrast possible narrative paths without claiming curves predict returns.

concepts.source_anchor: Equity is a stake in your story
concepts.draft_hook: Your startup pitch is also a bet employees are making.
concepts.explanatory_task: Explain cash-versus-equity opportunity costs as the author framework, without personal career or investment recommendations.

concepts.source_anchor: stock price going down a lot
concepts.draft_hook: A rising dividend yield can be a falling share price.
concepts.explanatory_task: Animate unchanged hypothetical dividend divided by a falling price; do not imply dividends are always bad.

concepts.draft_hook: Cash income is only part of your investment result.
concepts.explanatory_task: Show hypothetical price loss plus dividend; state taxes and timing assumptions and avoid bond-equivalence claims.

concepts.draft_hook: A high yield does not promise your next payment.
concepts.explanatory_task: Separate quoted yield from future cash payments; avoid old named-company payouts presented as current facts.

concepts.draft_hook: Before practicing harder, draw what you actually do.
concepts.explanatory_task: Animate an example process map and a weak step; present this as a decision tool.

concepts.draft_hook: Before deleting a process step, ask why it is there.
concepts.explanatory_task: Explain deliberate inclusion and exclusion with an original example, not borrowed imagery.

concepts.draft_hook: If you never log the change, hindsight writes your results.
concepts.explanatory_task: Show hypothesis, adjustment and recorded outcome; connect deliberately to this experiment without inventing success metrics.
